checkin_review.verdict: The plan's effectiveness has been limited by inconsistent adherence to both diet and training sessions. While sleep is good, the primary focus for the next phase is to simplify the plan to improve consistency and ensure all sessions are completed and calorie targets are met.
checkin_review.measured_trend: Your weight increased by 0.3 kg over 4 weeks (82 kg to 82.3 kg), which is an average gain of 0.075 kg per week. For an intermediate client aiming for muscle gain, the expected range is 0.076 to 0.114 kg per week. You are at the very bottom of this range.
checkin_review.real_tdee_estimate: Given the reported diet adherence of 50-70%, it is not possible to reliably estimate your actual TDEE from the measured weight trend. Your actual average calorie intake was likely significantly lower than the prescribed 3000 kcal, which explains the slow rate of gain. The current calorie target is appropriate if adhered to consistently.
checkin_review.calorie_change: The previous target of 3000 kcal will be maintained. The measured weight gain of 0.075 kg per week is at the lower end of the expected range for muscle gain, but due to the reported diet adherence of 50-70%, the primary issue is consistency rather than the target itself. Improving adherence to the current target is the priority.
training_changes: Barbell Bench Press has stalled at 60 kg x 8. The load will be reset by 10% to 55 kg for 3 sets of 5-8 reps to allow for a fresh progression.
Total weekly sets have been reduced from 85 to 63 to make sessions shorter and more manageable, aiming to improve training adherence from 'about half' to 100%.
Direct lateral delt and rear delt work has been added to both upper body days to ensure all major muscle groups are trained twice per week, addressing a previous programming gap.
keep_doing: Your sleep of 7-8 hours per night is excellent and provides a strong foundation for recovery and progress. Continue to prioritize this.
The 4-day Upper/Lower split is effective and well-suited to your availability; this structure will be maintained.

weekly_split.scheduling_note: Days are movable. Keep at least one day between the two upper sessions and between the two lower sessions, for example Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday as written, or Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Friday.

protocol: For each exercise, aim to hit the top of the prescribed rep range for all sets at the target RIR.
Once you achieve the top of the rep range for all sets (e.g., 3 sets of 8 reps when the range is 5-8), increase the load by the smallest increment possible in the next session.
When load is increased, reps will likely drop to the bottom of the range. Work to build them back up to the top of the range again.
If neither load nor reps improve for 2 consecutive sessions on a lift, despite adequate sleep and food, reduce that lift's load by 10% and rebuild.
progressive_overload.load_increments: Use 2.5 kg for upper-body barbell lifts, 5 kg for lower-body barbell lifts and machines, and the smallest available dumbbell increment (e.g., 1 kg or 2.5 lb per dumbbell).
progressive_overload.deload: A planned deload week will occur every 6 to 8 weeks. During a deload, halve your working sets and reduce the load by 15-20% for that week. This helps dissipate accumulated fatigue and prevents plateaus. An immediate deload is triggered if 2 or more lifts stall in the same week despite adequate sleep and food, or if you report persistently elevated soreness and falling motivation for 2 consecutive weeks.
progressive_overload.tracking: Log every session, including exercises, sets, reps, and loads. Track your body weight daily (using a 7-day average for trends), and measure your waist circumference and take progress photos every 2 weeks.

quality_vs_quantity.stance: Quality of execution and honest proximity to failure are paramount; these outweigh simply adding more sets or reps without purpose.
quality_vs_quantity.why: The primary stimulus for muscle growth occurs in hard sets performed with good technique, close to muscular failure (roughly 0 to 3 RIR). Sets performed with poor form, excessive momentum, or stopped 5 or more reps short of failure are 'junk volume' that adds fatigue without contributing significantly to muscle growth.
practical_rules: Prioritize perfect technique over lifting heavier weight. If form breaks down, the set ends.
Perform each rep with control, especially the lowering (eccentric) phase, typically a 2-second count.
Ensure you are truly working within the prescribed RIR. If a set feels easier than RIR 3, push for more reps or slightly more weight in the next session.
Rest adequately between sets (120-300 seconds for compounds, 60-90 seconds for isolation) to ensure performance is maintained across sets.
Do not add extra sets beyond the program unless you are consistently hitting the top of the rep range for all prescribed sets at the target RIR and still feel fresh.

rationale.exercise_selection: Exercises were selected to cover all major movement patterns (squat, hinge, horizontal press, horizontal pull, vertical press, vertical pull, single-leg) and include direct work for arms, delts, calves, and abs. High stimulus-to-fatigue exercises like chest-supported rows and seated leg curls are prioritized for efficient muscle growth. Face pulls and lateral raises were added to ensure comprehensive shoulder development and address previous frequency gaps for rear and lateral deltoids.
rationale.ordering: Compound movements are placed at the beginning of each session when energy levels are highest, allowing for maximal effort and progressive overload on the most impactful lifts. Isolation exercises are placed towards the end of the session.
rationale.volume_analysis: This revised plan targets the intermediate weekly volume landmarks (10-16 hard sets per muscle group). Quads: 18 sets (2x frequency). Hamstrings: 12 sets (2x frequency). Glutes: 12 sets (2x frequency). Chest: 10 sets (2x frequency). Vertical Pull (Back): 10 sets (2x frequency). Horizontal Pull (Back): 10 sets (2x frequency). Shoulders (Press): 10 sets (2x frequency). Lateral Delts: 4 sets (2x frequency). Rear Delts: 4 sets (2x frequency). Triceps: 4 sets (2x frequency). Biceps: 4 sets (2x frequency). Calves: 6 sets (2x frequency). Abs: 4 sets (2x frequency). Total weekly sets are 63, a reduction from the previous plan's 85 sets, aimed at improving adherence while maintaining effective training frequency and stimulus.
rationale.goal_fit: The plan is designed for muscle gain through hypertrophy-focused training. The 4-day Upper/Lower split provides adequate frequency for all muscle groups. The slight reduction in total volume is a strategic adjustment to improve adherence, which is critical for consistent progress towards muscle gain. The calorie surplus is maintained to support muscle growth, with the understanding that consistent adherence to this target is now the primary driver of progress.

cardio_and_steps.step_rationale: To support overall health, recovery, and maintain a lean physique during a muscle gain phase, your daily step target is increased from 6000 to 8000 steps. This is an increase of 2000 steps, which equates to approximately 20 minutes of additional walking per day.

cardio_sessions.intensity: Conversational pace (60-70% of max heart rate)
cardio_sessions.placement: 2 sessions per week, preferably on rest days (Wednesday, Saturday) or at least 6 hours away from lifting sessions.

cardio_and_steps.interference_note: At these prescribed doses, cardio is unlikely to interfere with muscle gain. Significant interference only becomes a concern with high volumes of endurance training.

diet_plan.macro_rationale: Protein is set at 2.0 g per kg of body weight (165 g for 82.3 kg) to support muscle protein synthesis and recovery, aligning with the Morton et al. 2018 meta-analysis. Fat is set at 1.0 g per kg of body weight (80 g) to support hormonal health. Carbohydrates fill the remaining calories (405 g) to fuel training performance and recovery. This macro split ensures a balanced intake for muscle gain.

meal_schedule.timing_note: Focus on a balanced start to the day.
Ensure adequate protein and carbs for sustained energy.
Consumed 2-3 hours before your evening training session, this meal provides critical fuel (carbs at 1-1.5 g/kg) and protein for performance.
Consumed within 1-2 hours post-workout to aid recovery and muscle repair. Focus on protein and carbohydrates.

sample_day_totals.note: These totals are within 5% of the daily targets. Equal-macro swaps with similar foods are encouraged for variety and adherence.

diet_plan.pre_post_workout: Consume a mixed meal (Meal 3) 2-3 hours before your workout, containing approximately 1-1.5 g of carbohydrates per kg of body weight and a full protein serving. Within 1-2 hours post-workout (Meal 4), consume a meal with 0.4-0.5 g of protein per kg of body weight plus carbohydrates to support recovery. The post-workout window is generous when a pre-workout meal has been consumed.
diet_plan.hydration: Aim for 30-40 ml of water per kg of body weight daily (approximately 2.5-3.3 liters for your weight), plus an additional 500-750 ml around training sessions. A practical check is pale straw-colored urine throughout the day.
diet_plan.diet_preference_note: This plan assumes a non-vegetarian diet based on the absence of specific preferences in your intake. All foods can be swapped for similar macro-nutrient profiles to suit your taste.
diet_plan.allergy_note: No allergies were reported in your intake form. If any allergies exist, please inform your coach immediately so the plan can be adjusted to exclude those ingredients.

supplements.name: Creatine Monohydrate
supplements.timing: Any time of day, no cycling required.
supplements.reason: Increases muscle phosphocreatine stores, enhancing high-intensity exercise performance, strength, and muscle mass (ISSN position stand). Expect a 0.5-1 kg increase in water weight.
supplements.caveat: Consult a physician before use if you have pre-existing kidney conditions or are on related medications.

supplements.name: Protein Powder (Whey or plant-based blend)
supplements.timing: As needed to meet daily protein target, especially post-workout or between meals.
supplements.reason: A convenient and efficient way to increase daily protein intake, supporting muscle repair and growth, particularly when whole food options are not practical. It is a food source, not a magic bullet.
supplements.caveat: Choose a plant-based blend (e.g., pea-rice) if you have dairy sensitivities or follow a vegetarian/vegan diet. Always prioritize whole food sources first.

supplements_excluded_note: Supplements such as SARMs, prohormones, testosterone boosters, fat burners, thermogenics, BCAAs/EAAs (when daily protein is adequate), glutamine for muscle growth, mass gainers, and proprietary blends are not recommended due to lack of strong evidence, potential health risks, or being unnecessary with an optimized diet. They are excluded from this plan.

duration_and_paths.duration_rationale: This plan is designed to be run consistently for 3 months. Adaptation requires a sustained, consistent stimulus, and program hopping before 12 weeks is a common reason for stalled progress. Deloads are already scheduled within this timeframe to manage fatigue.
duration_and_paths.review_points: Review your progress every 4 weeks by comparing your 7-day average body weight trend against the target gain of 0.076 to 0.114 kg per week, re-measuring your waist, and checking your training log for consistent increases in load or reps on your key lifts.

next_paths.name: Continue Muscle Gain (Next Phase)
next_paths.when_to_choose: Choose this path if you are consistently gaining muscle (0.076 to 0.114 kg per week on average), lifts are progressing, and body fat levels remain acceptable.
next_paths.what_changes: Increase calorie target by 100-200 kcal (primarily carbs), slightly increase weekly training volume by 1-2 sets for 1-2 priority muscle groups, and potentially introduce new exercise variations.

next_paths.name: Mini-Cut (Fat Loss Phase)
next_paths.when_to_choose: Choose this path if you have gained more body fat than desired, or if your rate of muscle gain has significantly slowed despite consistent adherence and progressive overload.
next_paths.what_changes: Reduce calorie target by 400-500 kcal (primarily carbs and fats), increase daily step target by 2000-4000 steps, and maintain current training volume and intensity to preserve muscle mass.

next_paths.name: Strength Block
next_paths.when_to_choose: Choose this path if your primary goal shifts to increasing absolute strength on key lifts, and you are comfortable with your current body composition.
next_paths.what_changes: Adjust rep ranges for primary lifts to 3-6 reps, maintain calorie intake at maintenance or a slight surplus, and potentially reduce overall training volume slightly to prioritize recovery for heavier loads.

safety_notes.medical_disclaimer: This program is for educational purposes and is not medical advice. Consult your physician before beginning any new exercise or nutrition program, especially if you have any pre-existing health conditions. Stop exercising immediately and seek medical attention if you experience chest pain, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or any other severe symptoms.
